SCENE 1
[Setting: Along the Rio Grande in West Texas.]

`bbtext(NARRATOR)`: [Talking to the audience.] Hello there, fellow Texans. We sure do love our state, don’t we? But even though we love it, we may not always know everything about it. Like for instance, did you ever wonder how the Rio Grande got that Big Bend in it? Well, even if you never did wonder that, you’re about to find out. Here come the makers of the Big Bend now!
[Enter Husband and Wife. They tend to their dry fields.]
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: [Entering.] Howdy, sir. Ma’am. Sure is a mighty fine `text(day)` today, wouldn’t you agree?
`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: [Grunting.] It most certainly is not a fine `text(day)`! These turnips need water!
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: I don’t see any turnips. And I don’t see any water, either.

`bbtext(WIFE)`: Exactly! We need some rain or some river water to irrigate our crops. But there’s not a drop around here. I’m starting to regret ever settling this farm. Maybe we’ll just move back east.
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: [Shaking head.] Now, don’t do anything hasty. There’s plenty of water to the south and west of here.
`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: There is? Where?
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: Why, in the Rio Grande, of course! But that’s `text(hundreds)` of `text(miles)` away. You’ll have to move your farm there. Well, I’ll be seeing you around. [Exits.]
`bbtext(WIFE)`: Move our farm? What a crazy idea. We like it here!
SCENE 2
`bbtext(NARRATOR)`: That night, the husband and wife had a talk.
`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: You know, I’ve been thinking about what that cowboy had to say this morning about the river.
`bbtext(WIFE)`: You’re not thinking of moving the farm, are you?

`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: [Shaking his head.] You know I don’t want to leave. We’ve worked too hard to get this place going. But the turnips need water, and there’s no water here. I don’t see any other choice.
`bbtext(WIFE)`: Well, I’ve been thinking, too. I think I know how we can stay here on our farm and have plenty of water.
[Wife and Husband huddle together and make plans.]
SCENE 3
`bbtext(NARRATOR)`: The next `text(day)`, the `text(two)` got to work on their plan.
`bbtext(WIFE)`: [Pointing to the boulders.] These are the perfect size. Let’s wrap the rope around this big one here and pull it into place.
`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: [Ties the rope around the boulder.] I think we’re getting stronger, pulling all these boulders. It’s getting easier all the time.
`bbtext(WIFE)`: You’re right! Given enough time, I bet we could move a mountain!
[Husband and Wife keep piling rocks higher and higher during the scene.]
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: [Entering the scene.] Well, howdy, again. What are you folks doing now?
`bbtext(HUSBAND)`: Howdy! After you mentioned the Rio Grande yesterday, we decided to take matters into our own hands.
`bbtext(COWBOY)`: Are you building a lake or something?
`bbtext(WIFE)`: Nope. We didn’t want to move our farm to the river, so instead, we’re moving the river to our farm. Now, if you’ll excuse us, we have a lot of work to do.

`bbtext(NARRATOR)`: Those `text(two)` worked and worked until they had built a canyon of rocks — to steer the river water, of course. After they had the rocks in place, they turned the waters of the Rio Grande to flow through their new canyon. And that’s how Big Bend was made. Now that there is the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And if I’m lying, may the sun go dark.
[All the lights on stage go out.]
`bbtext(NARRATOR)`: [In darkness.] Okay, maybe it wasn’t the whole truth.
[Curtain.]
